propositions.name: Better Elections Act (A Third Time) (BEAATA)
propositions.author: Representative-Fee65
propositions.text:
Section I - Bringing Back Mock Elections
Should this bill pass, mock elections will return to the election schedule, with the election chosen by either the ElSec or the subreddit.
Section II - New Election Schedule
Should this bill pass, the election schedule would be as follows after the September Class 7 election:
November: Mock Election
December: Class 2 and Class 3
January: Mock Election
February: Class 4 and Class 5
March: Mock Election
April: Class 6 and Class 7
May: Mock Election
June: Class 1 and Class 2
And so on.
This is expected to reduce the average term length by approximately 1-2 months and is projected to decrease the number of resignations as well as long periods of inactivity.
If a moderator resigns before their next election, the closest election day would be when the seat becomes available for a new election. (Ex: a moderator resigns in January after the last election, the next election would be held on in February, regardless of the mock election)

propositions.name: Elected Council Supremacy Amendment
propositions.author: practicalpurpose
propositions.text:
To better administer the sub government, reduce jurisdictional confusion, and establish the supremacy of a democratically elected Mod Council in our sub government, the Spinroom Constitution shall be amended to comply with the following:
The Mod Council shall be redefined as the collection of all Elected-Mods but shall no longer include Perma-Mods. This Council shall continue to function with all duties and responsibilities previously assigned to the Mod Council unless otherwise specified in this Amendment.
The Mod Council shall be considered a parliament, a representative house of the sub membership, and as such, serve as the unified supreme executive and legislative branch of the sub government. It shall also retain the power to pardon, commute sentences, and override other criminal justice decisions.
The Mod Council may create "bylaws" in accordance with powers granted to the Council by the Constitution or by Prop. All bylaws shall be a form of sub law inferior to Props and the Constitution. A Prop or Amendment may override a bylaw where applicable.
The "Mod Assembly" shall be created and be defined as the collection of all Mods. This Assembly shall be considered the supreme administrative branch of the sub, charged with managing the technical operation of the sub and its government.
Each Perma-Mod and each Elected-Mod shall have one vote on matters in the Mod Assembly.
Perma-Mods shall continue to serve as Justices of the Subreddit Supreme Court and may advise the Mod Council, but shall have no voting power on the Mod Council (except in the cases of certain ties).
In the event of a tied vote on the Mod Council, the matter shall be referred to the full Mod Assembly, which may attempt to break the tie. If the Assembly fails to break the tie, the motion or matter fails; otherwise, it passes.
Mod Council matters with special voting requirements beyond a simple majority, such as >75% approval of Councilors, may not be referred to the Mod Assembly for tie-breaking unless clarified by the special voting requirement.
The Mod Assembly, like the Mod Council, shall make decisions by majority rule, unless an alternative standard is prescribed by law. A majority is achieved when more than 50% of the eligible and participating Assembly voters in attendance cast their vote in the affirmative, provided that a quorum is present, proper notice has been issued, and ample time has been afforded for participation. An Assembly voter that chooses to abstain from a vote shall be counted for the purposes of a quorum but shall not be considered as a participant in the vote and therefore not counted in the total necessary for a majority.
If a matter or motion is referred to the Mod Assembly from the Mod Council, the Council's votes automatically carry-over to the Mod Assembly vote.
Remove "as an executive matter" from the line "The Mod Council may, by majority vote as an executive matter, overrule any Administrative Officer executive action."
Administrative Officers may nominate their replacements upon their resignation or removal from office, but the Mod Council, by majority assent, must approve the nomination before the nominee can assume the office (in addition to any other rules required).
A Perma-Mod, upon resignation or removal from office, may nominate their replacement but the Mod Council, by majority assent, must approve the nomination before the nominee can assume the office. If the Mod Council does not approve the nominee, the Perma-Mod position is eliminated. (Does not apply in case in the case of a Conclave)
For ceremonial purposes, the Mod Assembly is the upper house of government, and the Mod Council is the lower house of government.

propositions.name: Elections Secretary Conclave Amendment
propositions.author: practicalpurpose
propositions.text: The Elections Secretary shall be chosen by a Conclave of all Mods (by the Mod Assembly if the Elected Council Supremacy Amendment is passed) with an approval vote of two-thirds or greater. Once the position is accepted, an approved nominee may immediately assume the role of Elections Secretary and shall automatically be elevated to the rank of Perma-Mod. In the event that the Elections Secretary resigns or is otherwise removed from office, the Secretary must forfeit their Perma-Modship. If the selected is an Elected-Mod, the Elections Secretary automatically resigns their Elected-Mod position upon acceptance of the new position, and may nominate their successor in accordance with the regular resignation procedure. Unlike other Administrative Officers, the Elections Secretary may not be removed from office by a majority vote of the Mod Council, but instead must be impeached or recalled. Once created, the Office may not be eliminated except by a two-thirds vote of the Mod Council.
